report.refutation_basis: Both catalog-named probes were freshly rerun from executable source and hermetic paired fixtures. All three byte-threshold differentials reproduced and the zero-byte control discriminated in both states.
report.question_or_target: Does any scoring, ranking or gating rule in the program reward artifact size, token count or finding count - and would it penalise a correct falsification that produces almost no output?
report.answer: YES for artifact byte size. Three live acceptance rules penalize the small correct falsification (138 bytes) and accept its semantically identical padded twin (1755 bytes). No scoped rule rewards token count or finding count. Presence counts for evidence/tests/controls are semantic completeness checks, and exact byte counts in integrity gates are equality checks rather than more-is-better scores.
report.scope: All generic Prompt Two unit-output acceptance/accounting gates reachable from the R2E runner contract: the operative tail gate, both executable Gate-A reducers, the declared output schema, condition 11, and delivery reconciliation.

targets.finding: The operative runner rejects the 138-byte falsification before reading its exact completion marker and accepts the 1755-byte padded twin.
Condition 3 turns the same semantic result from INCOMPLETE to COMPLETE solely when padding crosses the declared byte minimum.
The second Gate-A reducer has the same condition-3 differential: padding alone changes the result to complete.
The structural schema does not rank greater byte volume higher; padding does not change a parse/schema outcome into a pass that the small arm lacked solely due to size.
Hermetic existence/hash recording accepts both paired non-empty artifacts and the empty file as a present path; this integrity gate records exact bytes but does not reward a larger value.
Delivery accounting accepts both non-empty arms and rejects only the genuinely empty arm; it does not rank greater byte volume higher.
